title: Virtualization
homeDescription: Review virtual machines, shared server resources, and Type 1 and Type 2 hypervisors.
studyGuideDescription: Practice identifying virtualization concepts and hypervisor types.

tabs.label: [QUESTIONS]
tabs.heading: [VIRTUALIZATION_CHECK]
tabs.description: Test your knowledge of virtual machines and hypervisor types.

questions.prompt: What does virtualization allow a computer to do?
options: Run multiple operating systems directly on physical hardware
Give one operating system exclusive access to all server resources
Replace the host operating system with a physical server
questions.explanation: Virtualization uses hypervisors to run a virtual operating system.

questions.prompt: Which is a benefit of using virtualization on a server?
options: Multiple virtual machines can share the server's resources
Each virtual machine can receive dedicated physical resources
Every virtual machine can use the full server without sharing resources
A virtual machine can run without a host operating system or hypervisor
questions.answer: Multiple virtual machines can share the server's resources
questions.explanation: Virtualization allows multiple virtual machines with different operating systems to share and use server resources.

questions.prompt: What can be transported to another physical server relatively easily with virtualization?
options: A backup of the entire virtual machine
A backup of the physical server's hardware
An image containing only the host operating system
A copy of the server's physical memory modules
questions.answer: A backup of the entire virtual machine
questions.explanation: Virtualization makes it easier to transport a backup of an entire virtual machine to another physical server.

questions.prompt: A hypervisor runs directly on the physical server hardware. Which type is it?
questions.explanation: Type 1 hypervisors are bare metal and run directly on the hardware.

questions.prompt: Which product is an example of a Type 1 hypervisor?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Hyper-V, VMware ESXi, Citrix XenServer, and ProxMox are listed as Type 1 examples.

questions.prompt: A hypervisor runs on an existing operating system, and both systems share resources. Which type is it?
questions.explanation: Type 2 hypervisors run on an existing operating system, so the host OS and virtual machine share resources.

questions.prompt: Which product is an example of a Type 2 hypervisor?
questions.explanation: VMware Workstation, Oracle VirtualBox, and MS Virtual PC are listed as Type 2 examples.
